important.name: Snapshot base breaks the lane review diff range
important.summary:
cut_base (parallel2.py:336-346) now cuts a later wave from an unreferenced commit S whose parent is HEAD and that holds the earlier waves' staged work. The skill's step 5 still reviews each returned lane with `git -C "<worktree>" diff <target>...HEAD` and claims the three-dot range starts at the lane's base commit. For a snapshot lane, merge-base(target, lane HEAD) is HEAD, not S, so the review diff also contains every staged earlier-wave change carried in S. Spec and quality reviewers of wave 2+ lanes then judge other lanes' work as this lane's and can send bogus findings back to the lane, which has no right to edit those paths.

Also (runtime): cmd_setup saves the lanes as dispatched (parallel2.py:383) and only then calls prepare_lanes, which loads d-w's new_worktree.py through dw_commands (349-357). A load failure raises CaptureError (or an uncaught import error) after the worktrees and state exist, so setup exits 1 without printing the notes, dispatch rows or probes; a rerun refuses because the wave is no longer planned. This contradicts the docstring's 'a failed step never fails setup' and leaves the operator to rebuild the rows from status.
fix: Change SKILL.md step 5 to diff from the lane's recorded base: `git -C "<worktree>" diff <base>..HEAD`, with `<base>` read from the base column `P2 status` prints (render_status_line already emits base_sha[:12]), and drop the claim that `<target>...HEAD` starts at the base commit.
Or have setup print the base SHA in each dispatch row / brief and have step 5 name that SHA explicitly.
Call dw_commands() once before cut_base/create_worktrees when args.with_setup is set, so a load failure refuses setup before anything is written, and pass the loaded prepare to prepare_lanes.
Or print print_notes/print_dispatch (and probes) before running prepare_lanes, whose output goes to stderr anyway.

important.name: Step 5 review range includes earlier waves' staged work for snapshot-cut lanes
important.summary:
SKILL.md step 5 (unchanged text, made false by this PR) tells the reviewers to read `git -C "<worktree>" diff <target>...HEAD` and says the three-dot range starts at the lane's base commit. With changes staged, `cut_base` (plugins/harness/scripts/parallel2.py:336-346) cuts the lanes from a snapshot commit whose parent is the target's HEAD. The merge base of the target and the lane is then the target's HEAD, not the snapshot, so the range also holds every staged earlier-wave change. The spec and quality reviewers of a later-wave lane review, and may flag, code that lane never wrote. `P2 status` already prints the base (`render_status_line`, plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/parallel_lanes.py:458-464), so the correct range is available.

Also (overall): SKILL.md step 5 has reviewers read `git -C "<worktree>" diff <target>...HEAD` and says the three-dot range starts at the lane's base commit. That held while lanes were cut from HEAD. With W1, `cut_base` (plugins/harness/scripts/parallel2.py:336-346) cuts a later wave from an index snapshot whose parent is the target's HEAD. The merge base of `<target>` and the lane branch is then the target HEAD, not the snapshot. The reviewed diff therefore holds every earlier wave's staged change plus any unrelated staged work, attributed to this lane. The spec-compliance and code-quality reviewers would review, and possibly send back, work the lane never touched. `stage` diffs from `base_sha`, so the staged result is correct; only the review contract broke.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md step 5 tells reviewers to read `git -C "<worktree>" diff <target>...HEAD` and says the three-dot range starts at the lane's base commit. That held while lanes were cut from HEAD. This PR cuts a later wave from an index snapshot (`cut_base`, parallel2.py, `snapshot_commit` with HEAD as parent), so the lane's base is the snapshot, not the target tip. `merge-base(<target>, lane HEAD)` is the target HEAD, which is the snapshot's parent. The range therefore also covers every staged earlier-wave lane and any staged developer change. The spec-compliance and code-quality reviewers get that work as if this lane wrote it. The driver's own `stage` diffs from `base_sha` correctly, so only the documented review range is wrong. `P2 status` already prints the base as the last column (`render_status_line`, parallel_lanes.py:458-464).

Also (roast): SKILL.md step 5 tells reviewers to read `git -C <worktree> diff <target>...HEAD` and says the three-dot range starts at the lane's base commit. When `setup` cuts a lane from an index snapshot (parallel2.py `cut_base` / `snapshot_commit`), the base is a commit on top of the target's HEAD that no branch references. merge-base(target, lane HEAD) is then the target's HEAD, not the snapshot, so the range also shows every staged earlier-wave change. Both reviewers get those changes as if the lane made them and may flag them as out-of-scope edits. The same lane is staged from `base_sha` (apply_lane), so what the reviewers read and what gets staged no longer match. Snapshots were added to make later waves cheaper, and they quietly make the review step wrong.

Also (docs): SKILL.md step 4 and the skill README Companion mod section say each lane starts with its worktree as its working directory. `laneCwd` (plugins/parallel2-lanes/hooks/lanes.ts:65-66) sets `cwd` only for an implement lane with a worktree; review and research lanes keep the session's directory. The mod's own README (line 15) states the restriction correctly.
fix: Rewrite the step 5 range as `git -C "<worktree>" diff <base>..HEAD`, where `<base>` is the last column of `P2 status` (the lane's base commit, the index snapshot when one was cut), and drop the three-dot sentence.

Rewrite step 5 to use the recorded base: `git -C "<worktree>" diff <base>..HEAD`, where `<base>` is the last column `P2 status` already prints (`render_status_line` in parallel_lanes.py). Drop the claim that the three-dot range starts at the lane's base.
Have the driver print the review command per lane (for example a `review: git -C <worktree> diff <base_sha>..HEAD` line in `status` or in the dispatch row), and point step 5 at it.

Rewrite SKILL.md step 5 to review `git -C "<worktree>" diff <base>..HEAD`, where `<base>` is the last column of `P2 status` (the lane's base commit: HEAD, or the index snapshot for a later wave). Drop the claim that `<target>...HEAD` starts at the base.
Alternatively, have `print_dispatch` (parallel2.py) print the lane's base SHA in the dispatch row and point step 5 at it.

Rewrite step 5 to diff from the recorded base: `git -C "<worktree>" diff <base>..HEAD`, where `<base>` is the base column `P2 status` prints. Drop the claim that the three-dot range starts at the base.
Or print the exact review command (base sha included) in each dispatch row or `status` line, and point step 5 at it.
Append 'for an implement lane' after 'its worktree as its working directory' in SKILL.md step 4 and after 'the lane worktree as its working directory' in the skill README Companion mod section.

important.name: test_parallel2.py never names new_worktree.py, so a d-w runner change skips the --with-setup test in PR CI
important.summary:
`dw_commands` (plugins/harness/scripts/parallel2.py:349-357) loads `skills/d-w/commands/new_worktree.py` with importlib from a path built at runtime, then calls its `prepare(cfg, path)`. `tools/select_tests.py` follows only import statements (`_direct_deps`). Its string-literal rule covers only non-`.py` data files (`data_readers`). So a change to `new_worktree.py`, such as a renamed `prepare` or a new signature, reaches `test_setup_with_setup_runs_the_project_setup_in_each_lane` by no route the selector sees. The test source does not contain `new_worktree` either. CLAUDE.md (Tests) requires a test that reaches a file by a runtime-built route to spell that file name in its source. Without the name, the pull request skips this test and only the full run after the merge to `main` catches the break.

Also (roast): `dw_commands` (parallel2.py:349) builds the path to `skills/d-w/commands/new_worktree.py` at runtime and loads it with `spec_from_file_location`, which is not an import that tools/select_tests.py follows. `test_setup_with_setup_runs_the_project_setup_in_each_lane` depends on that module's `prepare`, but tests/scripts/test_parallel2.py never spells `new_worktree`. A pull request that changes `prepare` (its signature or its output lines) will skip this test, and the break shows up only in the full run after the merge to main. CLAUDE.md requires such a test to spell out the file name. The selector is only as smart as the test lets it be.
fix: Name the file in the test source, for example a docstring on `test_setup_with_setup_runs_the_project_setup_in_each_lane` that reads: "Runs d-w's new_worktree.py prepare() in each lane." The selector's `mentions` matches the basename anywhere in the test text.
Name the file in the test's source, e.g. a docstring on test_setup_with_setup_runs_the_project_setup_in_each_lane: """`setup --with-setup` runs d-w's new_worktree.py `prepare` in each lane."""

minor.name: laneCwd ignores lane status
minor.summary:
laneCwd (lanes.ts:65-66) returns the recorded worktree for any implement lane, and laneSpawn sets it as the spawn cwd, without the status check the driver's has_live_worktree applies (status != cleaned). A brief dispatched for a cleaned lane spawns into a removed directory; if that spawn throws, the hook's catch handler (spawn.ts:65) reruns the original spawn without cwd, so an implement lane would run in the main checkout. An implement lane with no worktree (planned, stale brief) likewise passes with the brief inlined but no cwd.

Also (overall): `laneCwd` returns `lane.worktree` for any implement lane that has one. `clean_lane` in parallel2.py sets the status to `cleaned` but keeps the `worktree` field. The state file survives while other lanes stay live (default `cleanup` removes only staged lanes). An `Agent` call that reuses a cleaned lane's `Brief:` line, such as a follow-up fix after review, would then start with `cwd` set to a removed directory instead of passing through.

Also (system_shape): `laneCwd` (lanes.ts:65-66) returns the worktree of any implement lane that has a recorded worktree path. The driver's own rule for a live worktree, `has_live_worktree` (parallel_lanes.py:379-381), also requires status != `cleaned`. `cleanup --lane ID` keeps the state file and briefs while later waves are planned (`finish_state`), and `remove_worktree` leaves the path recorded. A later spawn with that lane's `Brief:` line would then start in a directory that no longer exists, instead of passing through the way the README's 'anything unreadable passes the spawn through unchanged' promises.

Also (roast): `laneCwd` returns `lane.worktree` for any implement lane that has one, whatever its status. `cleanup --lane` marks a lane `cleaned` and removes its worktree, but keeps the run state and briefs while other lanes remain, and the state still records the worktree path. A later Agent call that opens with that lane's `Brief:` line (for example a retry) is rewritten to use a directory that no longer exists as its cwd. That contradicts the mod's promise that anything unusable passes through unchanged. The status is right there in the state file, and nothing reads it.
fix: In laneCwd require `lane.status === 'dispatched'` (or at least not 'cleaned'), and in laneOfPrompt return undefined for an implement lane whose cwd is undefined, so such a spawn passes through unrewritten.
In plugins/parallel2-lanes/hooks/lanes.ts `laneCwd`, also require `lane.status !== 'cleaned'` (or `=== 'dispatched'`). Add a spawn.test.ts case where a `cleaned` lane keeps the session directory.

Make `laneCwd` require `lane.status !== 'cleaned'` (mirroring `has_live_worktree`), or have `laneOfPrompt` return undefined for a cleaned lane so the spawn passes through. Add a spawn.test.ts case for a cleaned lane.
Return undefined from `laneCwd` (or pass the spawn through in `laneOfPrompt`) when `lane.status === 'cleaned'`, and add a spawn.test.ts case for a cleaned lane.

minor.name: The 'unknown lane' pass-through case never isolates an unknown lane
minor.summary:
The test 'a missing brief, a missing state or an unknown lane passes through' spawns `Brief: .../ghost.md`, but the world has no ghost.md file. laneOfPrompt (spawn.ts:26-28) returns undefined because the brief is unreadable, so the case repeats the missing-brief case. The path where the brief reads but its lane is absent from the state never runs, and dropping the `lane === undefined` guard would go unnoticed here.

Also (tests): TASK-7 says forks, teammates and resumes pass through, and spawn.ts:19 (isOutOfScope) guards fork, isTeammate and workflow spawns. spawn.test.ts covers only prompt-based pass-through, and band.test.tsx covers only resume. A fork or teammate spawn whose prompt opens with a lane Brief line is never checked to keep its prompt, model and cwd.

Also (overall): `isOutOfScope` (spawn.ts:19) keeps the mod from rewriting fork, teammate and workflow spawns, and the README and module doc promise those pass through unchanged. spawn.test.ts covers prompts without a Brief line, missing files and a broken disk, but no spawn with `fork`, `isTeammate` or `workflow` set and a valid `Brief:` line. Dropping any of the three conditions would pass every test.

Also (roast): `isOutOfScope` (spawn.ts:19) is supposed to let forks, teammates and workflow agents pass through even when their prompt opens with a lane's `Brief:` line, and the mod README promises this. spawn.test.ts covers resumes (via band.test.tsx), missing briefs and a broken disk, but has no test where `fork`, `isTeammate` or `workflow` is set. Dropping the guard would break no test.
fix: Before the ghost spawn, add `w.files.set(`${FOLDER}/feat-x/ghost.md`, 'ghost brief')` so only the state lookup can fail, and assert that its prompt still starts with `Brief:`.

Add a spawn.test.ts case that spawns `{ ...dispatch(`Brief: ${BRIEF}`, 'sonnet'), fork: true }` (and one with `isTeammate: true`), then asserts the prompt is still `Brief: ...`, the model is sonnet and cwd is undefined.
Add a spawn.test.ts case that spawns with a valid `Brief:` line plus `fork: true` (and likewise `isTeammate`, `workflow`), and asserts that the prompt, model and cwd reach the engine unchanged.
Add a spawn.test.ts case that spawns a valid `Brief:` prompt with `fork: true` (and one with `isTeammate: true`), and asserts the prompt, model and cwd reach the engine unchanged.

minor.name: bubble-stamp contract test pins the marketplace's total mod count
minor.summary: test_claude_md_counts_eight_mods lives in the bubble-stamp registration test but asserts the repository-wide count, so every new mod has to edit another mod's contract test (as this change does). The count is not a bubble-stamp property.
fix: Move the count check to a repo-level contract test that derives the number of TypeScript mods from .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, compares it with the number word in CLAUDE.md, and keeps only the backticked-name checks here.

minor.name: Snapshot commit identity and the head_sha fallback are unchecked
minor.summary: The plan fixes the snapshot identity to `parallel2 <parallel2@localhost>` (values, source D1), and SNAPSHOT_IDENTITY (parallel2.py:80-83) sets it. test_setup_cuts_lanes_from_an_index_snapshot_when_changes_are_staged checks the snapshot's parent but not its author or committer, so a lost env overlay goes unseen wherever the test machine has a git identity. The moved_note fallback to base_sha for state without head_sha (TASK-1) also has no test.
fix: In the snapshot test, assert `git(project, "log", "-1", "--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>", item["base_sha"])` equals `parallel2 <parallel2@localhost>|parallel2 <parallel2@localhost>`.
Add a stage test that removes `head_sha` from the saved lane state, then asserts the `note: target moved` line after a target commit.

minor.name: setup --probe test does not check the 'exactly as probe --wave' contract
minor.summary: TASK-3 says `setup --probe` prints the wave's probe output exactly as `probe --wave <n>` would. The test checks only that the dispatch row comes before `probe=P1` and that one probe phrase appears. A drift between the two paths (a missing skip line, a different worktree, an extra blank line) would pass.
fix: After `run("setup", "--probe")`, run `probe --wave 1` and assert that `out` ends with that output.

minor.name: --with-setup test runs one lane and only the success path
minor.summary: The test is named 'runs the project setup in each lane', but it plans one lane, so it never shows that each implement lane is prepared or that each `lane <id>:` line comes before its own step lines. TASK-5 also says a failed step never fails setup, and no test covers that.
fix: Plan two implement lanes plus a review lane. Assert setup_ran.txt exists in both worktrees, and that err shows `lane task1:` before the first `setup [ok]` and `lane task2:` before the second.
Add a case whose worktree_setup command exits non-zero and assert setup still returns 0 with `setup [fail]` in err.

minor.name: probed_cover's same-folder rule has no test
minor.summary: `probed_cover` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/parallel_lanes.py:321-330) counts a probed lane only when its worktree sits in the same folder as the profile's worktree; its docstring states this as the safety condition for skipping a probe. `test_probe_skips_a_later_profile_covered_by_a_passed_probe` covers only the same-folder skip. No test proves a profile still gets a prompt when the earlier probed lanes sit in another folder (for example after `worktree_root` changes between waves), or when the probed tools cover only part of the profile. Deleting the folder comparison would pass every test.
fix: Add a test in tests/scripts/test_parallel2.py (or a unit test of `pl.probed_cover` in tests/lib): a lane probed in another folder does not cover, and partial tool coverage returns [] and prints the probe prompt.
